warning_texts: The swapped completion labels passed both machine gates. release_surface_gate binds each number to the anchor comment next to it, and gate_release_document checks only that the claim is present. No rule in audit/check_plan.json compares the words a reader sees with the claim_id they label.

release/report.md line 3 applies a delivered-only population to the whole page. A reader will take the completion rates (0.60 to 0.72) as shares among delivered orders, which is the wrong-denominator reading the spec's semantic traps warn about.
The dashboard only has caveats per card. Without n and population beside each estimate, the interval cannot be read as a sampling interval over a known count.

reconciliations and card_caveat_requirements in audit/release_surface_contract.json are empty, so the machine gate checked no reconciliation identity and no per-card context. I checked the identities myself (they hold); per-card context is covered only by this audit.
summary: Every figure on the page matches the registry and my own recomputation. But release/report.md prints the direct and partner completion rates under each other's names: line 14 says 'completion partner' but shows CLM-COMPLETION-DIRECT (0.724397, n = 24597), and line 16 says 'completion direct' but shows CLM-COMPLETION-PARTNER (0.604746, n = 19934). So a reader sees partner as the higher channel, while the test right below says a positive effect means direct is higher.
